To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) children who learn new skills quickly at the beginning of intensive home based ABA treatment for autism are more likely to be placed in less restrictive school environments, 2) children who learn quickly at the beginning are more likely to show less severe symptoms of ASD at the conclusion of treatment, and 3) children who learn more quickly at the beginning show greater gains in adaptive behavior.

The present study suggests the importance of initial learning rates in predicting outcome for children with Autism receiving early, intensive home based ABA intervention. 20 children were followed for 4 years after beginning treatment in the Rutgers Autism Program (RAP) a home based program.
initial learning rates were significantly related to outcome after 4 years for a group of children with autism receiving ABA intervention in home settings with parent coordination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of early, intensive, ABA based home programming for children with autism.
the effectiveness of intensive home based applied behavioral analysis programs for young children with autism.
the effectiveness of intensive home based ABA intervention in which the primary responsibility for program implementation and management is assumed by parents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intensive early ABA intervention is effective in increasing IQ scores, adaptive behavior, and decreasing autistic symptoms in children with autism.
intensive ABA programs have produced dramatic results for some children and more modest results for others, with a wide range of outcomes for children receiving the same type of intervention.
intensive behavioral programming has been shown to be effective in producing substantial improvements in the skills of children with autism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the home based programs are not as effective in terms of producing gains on standardized measures as are center based programs.
intensive home based programs have been shown effective, but the results of home based programs are variable.
the home based program is a good model for delivering services to young children with autism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
home based programs are feasible and can be effective.
the parents of children with autism can be trained to deliver intensive behavioral intervention in the home and that this model is a viable option to center based programming.
